content.stem: A force acts on an object. Name three effects that the force can have on the object.
content.answerKey: A force can change shape, change direction of motion, and accelerate or stop a body.
content.solution: A force can change the shape of the object. A force can change the direction in which the object is moving. A force can accelerate or stop a body.

content.stem: Write down a statement of Newton's second law of Motion (in words).
content.answerKey: Acceleration is in the direction of net force, proportional to that force and inversely proportional to mass.
content.solution: If a resultant force acts on a body, it will cause the body to accelerate in the direction of the resultant force. The acceleration of the body will be directly proportional to the resultant force and inversely proportional to the mass of the body.
